BRICS Cohesion Following Brazil’s Election

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has secured an unprecedented fourth term, an outcome analysts describe as a stabilizing force for the BRICS alliance. As a founding architect of the bloc, Lula’s return ensures Brazil remains committed to the partnership, countering previous concerns that his rival, Flavio Bolsonaro, might pivot the nation closer to Washington and away from BRICS’ strategic goals.

Global Policy Implications

Experts suggest Lula’s victory strengthens the grouping’s pursuit of a multipolar world order. While the bloc remains diverse with varied economic interests, the focus is shifting from political discourse to practical financial cooperation, including promoting trade in local currencies to reduce reliance on the US dollar. Despite these ambitions, researchers note that internal differences persist.
